meta.title: Topophany — the appearance of a place
meta.description: Self-hosted network topology and service availability monitoring in one Go binary. From where, via which path, reaching what — and on what evidence.
meta.og-description: From where, via which path, reaching what — and on what evidence. Self-hosted network monitoring with a terminal UI, in one Go binary.
nav.label: Main
hero.lede.html: From where, via which path, reaching what — and on what evidence.
hero.sub: Self-hosted monitoring of network topology and service availability, read in the terminal. One Go binary with no dependencies is the client, the collector and the observer. It tells you what was measured, from where and how recently. It never shows a check as green that hasn't passed.
hero.globe: A dotted globe turning slowly. Lit places are joined by paths: healthy paths faint with pulses running along them, one failing path red and dashed.
demo.lead.html: The Overview answers before you read a word: a verdict, a map of every place and path, and the short list of what needs attention. Below is topo preview recorded frame by frame from the TUI's own renderer. The evidence is synthetic, but it goes through the real state engine.
demo.recording: Recording of the Topophany terminal UI
demo.figcaption: A recording of the Topophany terminal UI in preview mode, in chapters that can be chosen below.
chapter.outage.title: An outage arrives
chapter.outage.text: All is well until x switches the preview to a scenario where the DMIT line is blocked from mainland China. Checks fail one sample at a time, and only confirmed failures turn red. Shown as a time-lapse.
chapter.route.title: Follow the route
chapter.route.text: Select something that needs attention and its whole route lights up on the map. Enter opens the evidence behind it.
chapter.vantage.title: Two vantage points
chapter.vantage.text: The same moment, viewed from two observers. From the MacBook in Changsha the line is down. From the server in New York every check passes. Each observer reports only what it can see from where it is.
chapter.virtual.title: Virtual geo
chapter.virtual.text: A schematic of the world that keeps its order but not its distances. A crowded city gets as much room as a lone island, and a glint runs along each wire whose traffic gets through.
chapter.geo.title: Geo
chapter.geo.text: A braille dot-matrix world map from Natural Earth. Nodes sit where you declared them, never where an IP lookup guesses.
chapter.network.title: Network
chapter.network.text: A layered schematic with sources on the left and each link one column further. Crossings are bridged, and hosted-in relations are dotted.
chapter.servers.title: Servers
chapter.servers.text: A card for every server: its services and the edge in front of each, its addresses by network, the containers and VMs it hosts, and your notes as a memo at the foot.
chapter.incidents.title: Incidents
chapter.incidents.text: Each incident lists the checks that failed and what other observers still see. A guess is labeled as a hypothesis, not a finding.
chapter.about.title: About
chapter.about.text: τόπος, place, and φαίνω, to bring to light. A globe on which the places you declared are the only lights.
demo.keys.html: 1–9 chapters m map v view x scenario space pause, or click the tabs inside the terminal. Run topo preview to try the real thing.
evidence.title: Evidence, not colors
evidence.lead.html: Health, the source of the evidence and its freshness are separate fields. Nothing turns green without a passing check, a service nobody monitors stays unknown, and a cached view says so.
green.title: Nothing is green by default
green.site-edge: answered by Cloudflare NRT · cache DYNAMIC
green.text.html: The state column stays empty for healthy rows, so problems are the only words lit. A service that is registered but has no check is not up. It is registered, not monitored.
vantage.title: Vantage points are explicit
vantage.label: From Changsha the path to the server in Los Angeles times out; from New York it answers with HTTP 200. Verdict: a fault on Changsha's path, not a server outage.
vantage.verdict: fault on the path from Changsha · server up
vantage.text: Each observer measures from where it actually is. A failure seen from home is a fault on that path, not a server outage, and the incident shows which observers still get through.
edge.title: The edge answered
edge.text: Behind Cloudflare, Vercel or another CDN, any answer from the edge, even an error page, proves the edge. The origin counts only a passing response the edge did not serve from cache. The probe records which edge answered and from where.
guess.title: A guess is labeled a guess
guess.label: An incident's evidence
guess.text: Incidents carry the failed checks and what other observers still see. Nothing is inferred about ports or protocols that nobody tested.
claims.title: What it will not claim
claims.tcp-means: Only that a connection was established. Not the application protocol, not proxy authentication, not the whole path.
claims.exit: A request succeeds, but the egress IP is outside policy
claims.exit-means.html: A policy outcome. Reachability and egress policy are judged separately.
claims.observer-means: Its view goes stale, then unknown. Remote assets are not marked down.
claims.candidate: The primary path fails, a candidate succeeds
claims.candidate-means: The candidate is available and redundancy is degraded. It does not claim production traffic has switched.
claims.collector-means: The cached view is kept, marked CACHED, and every item turns unknown.
arch.title: One binary, three roles
arch.lead.html: No CGO, no database daemon, no Node.js, and zero external Go modules. topo is the terminal client, the collector and the observer, and closing the client does not stop monitoring.
arch.label: Workers at each vantage point send observations to two independent collectors, which the read-only TUI clients query.
notes.collectors-text: Workers deliver to both collectors on their own and buffer in a bounded outbox. Duplicates are dropped by observation ID, and records from a mismatched configuration revision are quarantined.
notes.readonly-text.html: There is no remote configuration API, no remote shell and no automated remediation. Topology lives in reviewed local JSON, edited with topo edit and checked with topo validate.
notes.bounded-text: By default it keeps 24 hours or 20,000 raw records and gives the worker outbox 32 MiB. When a quota fills, probing stops with an error rather than dropping evidence.
probes.title: What it measures
probes.lead: Native probes and explicit proxy chains, plus read-only adapters for the tools already on your hosts.
probes.http: HTTP · status, body, headers, egress IP
install.title: Up in a minute
install.lead.html: Prebuilt archives for Linux, macOS and Windows, or one go install. The demo probes only its own loopback API and generates fresh credentials each time it runs.
install.go: Needs Go {{site.go}} or newer. Building downloads no modules.
install.archives.html: Archives for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, each with SHA256SUMS.txt.
runs.title: Runs on
runs.services-value: systemd units for the collector and the worker
runs.storage-value: a local append-only journal, no database
steps.look-text.html: The full TUI on a built-in topology with synthetic evidence. Press <kbd>x</kbd> to break something.
steps.collector-text.html: Writes a demo topology and fresh credentials, then serves on 127.0.0.1:7447.
steps.tui-text.html: In another terminal. Later, topo login saves a remote profile, and then plain topo is enough.
footer.fine: This site sets no cookies and loads nothing from anyone else.
